links.outcome: Rate of hallucinations, inaccuracies, and omissions in LLM-generated hospital courses
links.effect: Hallucinations in 21% (95% CI 14%-29%), inaccuracies in 41% (53/129; 95% CI 33%-50%), omissions in 24% (31/129; 95% CI 17%-32%) of 129 hospital courses.
links.quote: Hallucinations occurred in 21% (95% CI, 14%-29%) of the hospital courses, inaccuracies in 41% (53/129; 95% CI, 33%-50%), and omissions in 24% (31/129; 95% CI, 17%-32%).

links.outcome: Clinician review of real AI outputs for errors and perceived potential harm
links.effect: Errors were common (hallucinations 21%, inaccuracies 41%, omissions 24%), but perceived harm ratings were low (median 0; IQR 0-1), even assuming use without clinician correction.
links.quote: In this pediatric evaluation of LLM-generated hospital courses reviewed by frontline clinicians, errors were common, but perceived potential harm was low, even assuming use without clinician correction.

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy, quality, and potential harm of an EHR-integrated LLM drafting hospital courses during clinical implementation with clinician reviewers, but does not compare outcomes with vs without a specific guardrail practice.
